> **Endpoint is the base URL**, not the ingest path. Every SDK appends `/api/v1/events` itself — pass `http://localhost`, not `http://localhost/api/v1/events`. (Posting to the doubled path 404s, and older SDK versions reported that as success.) Only the raw `curl` example below uses the full URL.
> The API key above is scoped to **ingest** only (event tracking). It is deterministic and will be identical on every visit. No apiKey is stored server-side.

> **One key, all environments.** Use the same API key and project across development, staging, and production. Tag each event with `"environment": "dev"` (or `"staging"`, `"prod"`, etc.) — aliases are normalised server-side. The dashboard lets you filter to a single environment so your dev traffic never pollutes production numbers.
- **Custom events** — call `fb.track("event-name", { key: "value" })` for any user action
- **Funnel steps** — define funnels in the admin UI after approval; FunnelBarn will analyse conversion rates and drop-off
- **Session recordings** — enable `recording: true` in the JS SDK; rrweb captures full DOM mutations and replays them in the dashboard
- **Feature flags** — evaluate release/experiment flags at runtime via `POST /api/v1/evaluate` (see below)
> **Do not use** `x-api-key`, `Authorization`, or `X-Api-Key` — the server returns 401.
> The auth header must be `X-FunnelBarn-Api-Key` (HTTP header names are case-insensitive).
> Project routing reads `X-FunnelBarn-Project` only — do not put the project.Slug in the request body.
| `name` | string | **yes** | Event name — e.g. `page_view`, `cta_clicked`. Field is `name`, NOT `event`, `type`, or `event_name` |
| `session_id` | string | no | Persist this client-side across page loads. Omitted → server derives one from IP+UA (page-scoped only — no proper session stitching). |
| `user_id` | string | no | Stable identifier for a logged-in user. **Hashed server-side** (SHA-256) — the raw value is never stored. Same user → same hash, so funnels and cohorts still work. |
| `timestamp` | ISO 8601 string | no | Defaults to server receive time. Send your own for back-dated / batched events. |
| `url` | string | no | Page URL. **UTM params in the query string are auto-extracted** — you don't need to also pass them in `utm_*` fields. |
| `user_agent` | string | no | Overrides the `User-Agent` request header. Useful for server-side ingest where the UA header reflects your backend, not the end user's browser. |
| `properties` | object | no | Arbitrary key/value pairs — strings stay strings, numbers stay numbers. The main extension point for custom analytics. |

| `utm_source` / `utm_medium` / `utm_campaign` / `utm_term` / `utm_content` | string | no | Explicit override of values auto-extracted from `url`. Send these only when the URL doesn't already carry them. |

| `environment` | string | no | Deployment environment. Aliases are normalized: `prod`/`prd`/`live` → `production`, `stg`/`stage`/`acc`/`acceptance` → `staging`, `testing`/`tst`/`qa`/`uat`/`pr` → `test`, `dev`/`local`/`develop` → `development`. Omit for production (default). |
> Fields not listed above (`event`, `type`, etc.) are silently discarded.

Session recording captures full DOM snapshots and mutations using [rrweb](https://github.com/rrweb-io/rrweb).
Recordings are streamed in compressed chunks and can be replayed frame-by-frame in the dashboard.
Recording is **browser-only** — server-side SDKs do not generate recording data.
Two independent switches control whether a session is recorded:
1. **Client-side**: `recording: true` in the JS SDK (or `data-recording="true"` on the script tag)
2. **Server-side**: the admin dashboard can override the client setting — set the project's recording toggle to on/off, or adjust the sample rate
On every SDK init the browser fetches `GET /api/v1/recording-config` (no auth required for the call, the API key is used to scope the response to your project).
- If `enabled` is `false` the SDK stops any active recording, regardless of the client-side setting.
- `sample_rate` is a float in `[0, 1]`. The SDK rolls `Math.random()` once per page load and skips recording if the roll exceeds the rate. At `1.0` every session is captured.
- `rules` is an ordered list of URL-path glob rules checked for each chunk flush (first match wins, default is capture).
Rules let you restrict recording to specific paths or exclude sensitive pages without a code deploy.
1. SDK `recordExclude[]` — always suppresses recording for matching paths
3. Server rules (first match wins) — set in the admin dashboard
Pattern syntax: `*` matches any single path segment, `**` matches any number of segments.
// Capture checkout flows, never capture account or billing pages:
- **Password fields** are automatically masked as `***` — no apiKey credentials captured.
- Add the CSS class `fb-block` to any element you want fully redacted from recordings:
The JS SDK posts chunks automatically. If you are building a custom recorder or replaying your own rrweb stream, post directly:
| `recording_id` | string | Stable 32-hex-char ID for the recording. Generate once per page load; a new recording starts on each navigation. |
| `session_id` | string | Same session ID used for event tracking. Ties the recording to the user's session. |
| `chunk_index` | int | Zero-based, increments per flush within the same `recording_id`. The server uses this to track the first chunk index and total chunk count. |
| `events` | array | Array of `rrweb.eventWithTime` objects captured since the last flush. Must not be empty. |
| `started_at` | ISO 8601 string | Timestamp of when this recording started (i.e. when rrweb `record()` was called). |
| `duration_ms` | int | Elapsed milliseconds since `started_at` — used to compute `ended_at` and total session length. |

> **Note**: `page_url` is not in the request body. The server reads the `Referer` header and user-agent for metadata. Chunks are stored as gzip-compressed JSON in object storage; metadata (session, device type, duration) is stored in the database.

FunnelBarn doubles as a feature-flag service. Create flags in the admin
UI (release / experiment, with optional targeting rules and gradual
rollouts), then evaluate them at runtime from your app.
| `flag_key` | string | **yes** | The flag's key as configured in the dashboard |
| `default_value` | any | no | Returned when the flag is missing or eval errors. Also the value the flag is auto-registered with — see below. |
| `context` | object | no | User/session attributes for targeting + bucketing |
| `kind` | string | no | `experiment` (default) or `config`. Honoured only when this call auto-registers the flag. |
> **Important**: the `context` object is what targeting rules and the
> split-based bucketing read. Use the key `targeting_key` (or `session_id`)
> for the value that should stay sticky per user. `user_id` is **not**
> the bucket key — if you only send `user_id`, every call buckets the same
> way regardless of who the user is.
- `SPLIT` — no targeting rule matched, bucketed by `targeting_key` against the split percentages.
- `TARGETING_MATCH` — a rule matched. `flag_metadata.evaluated_rule_name` tells you which one.
- `STATIC` — a **config** flag: one value for everyone, no bucketing. See below.

- `DISABLED` — the flag is paused or not yet activated. You get **the flag's own default variant value**, not the `default_value` you sent. The two differ, and the difference is the point: an auto-registered flag is configurable from the dashboard before anyone activates it.
- `ERROR` — something went wrong; check `error_code` (e.g. `FLAG_NOT_FOUND`, `AUTO_REGISTER_LIMIT`). `value` echoes back the `default_value` you supplied.
Errors are returned as HTTP 200 with `reason: ERROR` and the supplied
`default_value` echoed back — never throw on missing flags, fall back.
`cache_max_age_seconds` is how long you may reuse this result without
re-evaluating; the same value is sent as `Cache-Control`. It is the one
sanctioned polling interval, so every consumer doesn't invent its own.
`0` means do not cache — an experiment resolves per targeting key and every
read is a data point, so caching one would both mis-bucket and silently
**Bucketing is deterministic.** A given `(flag_key, targeting_key)` pair
always resolves to the same variant — across calls, across processes,
across deploys. That's what makes A/B tests sticky and rollouts
modulo 10000, walked against split percentages in sorted variant order.
A flag is either an **experiment** or a **config** value. Pick the one that
matches how it is read — the kind decides the evaluation semantics, not just
| Read by | a user request | a server, often on a loop |
| Resolution | bucketed by `targeting_key` | one value for everyone |
| Evaluation rows | one per read | none |
| Variant / conversion report | yes | not shown |
Use `config` for a rate limit, a batch size, a daily cap — anything with no
user, no bucket and no conversion. A single value polled every 60s from three
pods writes ~4.3k evaluation rows a day as an experiment, all of them junk,
and they drown the flag's own analytics in machine reads.
### Values are arbitrary JSON, not just booleans
A variant's value can be a boolean, a number, a string, or a whole object.

### Evaluation context — send more, target better
The `context` object is a plain key/value map. There is no fixed schema —
pass whatever is meaningful at the call site. The richer the context, the
more specific the targeting rules you can write in the dashboard.
| Key | Example value | Why it helps |
| `targeting_key` | `"user-42"` | **Required for sticky bucketing.** Omitting it makes every call land in the same bucket. |
> **Consistency is what matters.** A key you send on 60% of calls can
> only be matched by a targeting rule for that 60%. Send the keys you
> care about on every call — even as empty string if the value is unknown.
> **Feedback loop.** FunnelBarn records which context keys appear in
> evaluations. In the targeting-rule editor, the context key field
> autocompletes from your real traffic and shows each key's inclusion
> rate (e.g. `plan — 94%`). The more consistently you send a key, the
> more prominently it surfaces. This makes the setup doc and the rule

### Reading and toggling flags from a service
Evaluation (above) tells a client what *it* resolves. To report what the
project actually holds — and to change it — use a **project-scoped flag
token**. That distinction matters: "the flag is off" and "the flag does not
exist and you are seeing your own default" are very different answers.
Create one in the dashboard under **Settings → API Keys**, with scope:
| `flags:read` | list and read this project's flags |
| `flags:write` | the above, plus update an existing flag (enable / disable / change its value) |
Tokens are bound to one project, hashed at rest, revocable, and carry a
last-used timestamp. Neither scope can **create or delete** a flag:
auto-registration already covers creation, and a token that can turn a gate
off should not also be able to delete the gate.
